run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend since 2026-11-15T06:44:24Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The RequestErrorRate alert on otel-demo/frontend traces to a configuration-only rollout of the shipping Deployment at 06:43:04Z. The new ReplicaSet shipping-5ffdc77bc8 sets QUOTE_ADDR=quote:0000, while the previous ReplicaSet shipping-75d58f5d84 used QUOTE_ADDR=http://quote:8080 (same image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-shipping, so only configuration changed). From that minute, every shipping /get-quote server span errors and its outbound quote client span is replaced by a failing span named 'POST ' with Http(http::Error(InvalidUri(InvalidFormat))). The failure propagates: checkout oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder returns gRPC status 13 INTERNAL ('shipping quote failure: failed POST to email service: expected 200, got 500') and frontend POST /api/checkout returns HTTP 500, which is the frontend error rate the alert reports. Quote and email show no error evidence of their own; email simply stops receiving order confirmations once the checkout flow aborts before it. The exact failing URL is not observable (not in span tags, and the shipping container logs only 'Requesting quote'), so the malformed-QUOTE_ADDR explanation rests on the exact onset plus the single template delta; the wrapped message's mention of the email service returning 500 could not be corroborated.

claims.text: Over 05:44:24-06:58:29 the frontend's error spans are confined to four checkout-path operations - 'POST', 'POST /api/checkout', 'executing api route (pages) /api/checkout' and 'grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder' - at roughly 428 error-span increase each; every other frontend operation returned 0 error spans (e.g. GET, GET /api/cart, GET /api/data, POST /api/cart, grpc.oteldemo.CartService/GetCart all 0).

Frontend error-span rate is 0 for all operations at every point from 06:19:24 through the 06:44:24 point, turns non-zero at the 06:45:24 point (0.170/s) and stays between 0.156/s and 0.585/s to the 06:57:24 point - an onset in the minute after the 06:43:04 shipping rollout, just before the 06:44:24 alert start.

The checkout service's own error spans are 'oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder' (~425) and 'HTTP POST' (~425); the same result shows its calls to oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge (~979), oteldemo.CurrencyService/Convert (~3548), oteldemo.CartService/GetCart (~1408), oteldemo.ProductCatalogService/GetProduct (~2569) and 'orders publish' (~979) only as STATUS_CODE_UNSET, with no ERROR series for those operations.

A sampled checkout error trace (trace_id 36e4c651c4ab2372d0ad5f57ced69aa6) shows frontend 'POST /api/checkout' with error=true and http.status_code 500 and exception.message '13 INTERNAL: shipping quote failure: failed POST to email service: expected 200, got 500'; checkout 'oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder' error with rpc.grpc.status_code 13 and otel.status_description 'shipping quote failure: failed POST to email service: expected 200, got 500'; shipping '/get-quote' error with otel.status_description 'Internal Server Error'; and shipping child span named 'POST ' with otel.status_description 'Http(http::Error(InvalidUri(InvalidFormat)))'.

In the same sampled frontend error traces, the frontend spans carry http.status_code 500 on 'POST', 'POST /api/checkout' and 'executing api route (pages) /api/checkout', and the frontend client span 'grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder' carries otel.status_code ERROR with rpc.grpc.status_code 13; no error detail is present on the frontend spans themselves.

The deepest visible failure is shipping's outbound call: shipping's server span '/get-quote' is marked error with 'Internal Server Error' and its only child is the span 'POST ' with 'Http(http::Error(InvalidUri(InvalidFormat)))' lasting 10 microseconds - a request-URI construction failure before any HTTP exchange - and no quote or email span appears beneath it in that trace.

Shipping span metrics: '/get-quote' has ~979.4 STATUS_CODE_UNSET and ~426.3 STATUS_CODE_ERROR; the client span 'POST ' has ~426.3 STATUS_CODE_ERROR; 'POST quote' has ~979.4 STATUS_CODE_UNSET; '/ship-order' has ~979.4 STATUS_CODE_UNSET.

Shipping '/get-quote' STATUS_CODE_ERROR is 0 at every point through 06:44:24 and then 0.34-0.53/s at the 06:45:24-06:51:24 points, while STATUS_CODE_UNSET is 0.20-0.62/s up to and including 06:44:24 (0.20 at that point) and 0 from 06:45:24 onward - i.e. the success series stops exactly when the error series starts.

Shipping's client-span mix switches at the rollout: 'POST quote' runs 0.36-0.51/s through the 06:44:24 point (0.20 there) and is 0 from the 06:46:24 point onward, while the failing 'POST ' span is 0 before 06:44:24 and 0.42-0.47/s at the 06:46:24, 06:48:24, 06:50:24 and 06:52:24 points.

Two shipping ReplicaSets exist: shipping-75d58f5d84 created 06:06:33Z (spec replicas 0) with QUOTE_ADDR=http://quote:8080, and shipping-5ffdc77bc8 created 06:43:04Z (spec replicas 1, ready 1) with QUOTE_ADDR=quote:0000; both use image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-shipping, so the 06:43 change was configuration-only.

Rollout events for shipping: pod shipping-5ffdc77bc8-755zn Scheduled 06:43:04Z, image Pulled 06:43:09Z, container Created 06:43:09Z, Started 06:43:11Z; ReplicaSet shipping-5ffdc77bc8 SuccessfulCreate 06:43:04Z; the old pod shipping-75d58f5d84-gw77q was Killing at 06:43:11Z with SuccessfulDelete; Deployment shipping shows ScalingReplicaSet up 06:43:04Z and down 06:43:11Z.
The only ReplicaSet created anywhere in namespace otel-demo after 06:40:00Z is shipping-5ffdc77bc8 at 06:43:04Z, so no other workload in that namespace was rolled out in the minutes before the alert.

The quote Service is exposed on port 8080 with targetPort 8080 (as are the shipping and email Services), so the new QUOTE_ADDR value's port 0000 points at a port the quote Service does not expose, and the value also omits the http:// scheme the old value had.

Over the whole window, error-span increase by service is: frontend 1713.6, frontend-proxy 888.3, shipping 852.6, checkout 850.5, recommendation 4.06, ad 3.05, fraud-detection 3.05, accounting 0, cart 0, payment 0; currency, product-catalog, email, quote, image-provider and kafka returned no error-series entries in this view.

Impact grouping with each entity's own failure evidence: affected - frontend (HTTP 500 error spans on the checkout path, ~1713 error spans), checkout ('oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder' and 'HTTP POST' error spans, ~850), shipping ('/get-quote' and 'POST ' error spans, ~852, the deepest failing component), and frontend-proxy (888.3 error spans; sampled 'ingress' and 'router frontend egress' spans carry error=true and http.status_code 500, propagated from the frontend 500 rather than originated there).

Checked with no failure evidence of their own: quote's returned span series are all STATUS_CODE_UNSET (POST /getquote, calculate-quote and {closure}, ~979.6 each) with no ERROR series; email's returned series are also all STATUS_CODE_UNSET and its 'POST /send_order_confirmation' rate falls from 0.48/s at 06:44:24 to 0 at the 06:49:24 and 06:54:24 points, matching the checkout flow aborting before email; checkout's sampled cart, currency and product-catalog calls carry rpc.grpc.status_code '0' (currency also otel.status_code 'OK'); and all 21 otel-demo pods are Running/Ready with 0 restarts, the shipping pod having no previous terminated container.

The shipping container's readable log output (newest 100 of 339 lines, 06:49:12-06:52:05Z) consists solely of 'Requesting quote' lines; no error, URI or exception text is visible in that sample, so the application does not log the outbound failure.

The failing requests do not show an email-side failure: no email span appears in the failing sampled traces, shipping's failing outbound span ends in 10 microseconds with a URI-parse error rather than an HTTP response, and email's own series show no errors with its request rate simply dropping to 0 after the checkout flow aborts.

Leading cause: the 06:43:04Z configuration-only shipping rollout replaced QUOTE_ADDR=http://quote:8080 with quote:0000 (no scheme, port 0000 instead of the quote Service's 8080), so shipping can no longer build a valid URI for its quote POST - observed as Http(http::Error(InvalidUri(InvalidFormat))) - which makes /get-quote return Internal Server Error, checkout PlaceOrder fail with gRPC 13, and frontend /api/checkout return HTTP 500, producing the frontend error-rate alert. The exact URI string is not exposed in span tags or logs, so the link rests on the exact temporal coincidence and the single pod-template delta.

Unresolved alternative: the wrapped checkout error says the failed POST was to the email service and that it expected 200 but got 500, which would make an email-service 5xx a second candidate cause; this is not corroborated - email shows no error spans/series and the visible shipping client span fails URI parsing before any response - but the literal target URL of the 'POST ' span cannot be read, so an email-targeted variant of the malformed-address problem cannot be fully excluded.

A failure of the quote service as the cause of shipping's /get-quote errors is not supported: quote's returned span series are all STATUS_CODE_UNSET with no ERROR series, and shipping's failing span is its own client-side URI-format error rather than an error status returned by quote.

The small error-span rates on ad, fraud-detection and recommendation are not tied to this incident: each shows about 0.0037-0.0038/s error spans at the 06:34:24 point (before the rollout) as well as at the 06:44:24 and 06:54:24 points (after it), i.e. a steady baseline on both sides of the 06:43:04 change.

Roll the shipping Deployment back to the previous pod template, or set QUOTE_ADDR back to http://quote:8080 (scheme plus the quote Service's real port, as in shipping-75d58f5d84), then verify that shipping /get-quote error spans stop and frontend POST /api/checkout returns 200.

Add logging of the outbound URL (or the resolved address) on client/URI errors in the shipping service so InvalidUri failures are diagnosable from pod logs, and review the delivery path that produced the shipping Deployment change at 06:43:04Z so the configuration error is caught before rollout.

gaps: change_history is not integrated in this Run, so who or what changed the shipping pod template at 06:43:04Z, and the intended change, cannot be established beyond the observed ReplicaSet/template diff.

The alerting rule 'RequestErrorRate' could not be retrieved: list_prometheus_rules returned no rules for that name and no rules at all, so the alert expression, threshold and the reported current value 1.7777777777777777 are unverified.

The exact failing URI string and the target service of shipping's 'POST ' span are not present in the visible span tags; the shipping application logs only 'Requesting quote' (a filtered error search returned no data, which is not proof of absence).
Frontend and email container logs returned 0 bytes, so the frontend 500s and any email-side 5xx are established only from span metrics/traces, not from application logs.

Traces are a biased, incomplete sample (the checkout error query reported incomplete=true), and traces_span_metrics_calls_total counts spans, not unique requests, so no complete call graph or per-request failure rate can be claimed.
The conflict between the wrapped message 'failed POST to email service: expected 200, got 500' and the observed URI-parse failure cannot be resolved with the available evidence.
next_steps: Revert the shipping Deployment to QUOTE_ADDR=http://quote:8080 (or the prior template) and watch shipping /get-quote errors and frontend POST /api/checkout status for recovery.
Retrieve the change/CI history for the shipping Deployment around 2026-11-15T06:43:04Z to confirm who changed QUOTE_ADDR and to what intent.
Confirm the expected QUOTE_ADDR format for the ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-shipping image against its configuration documentation before re-applying.
Instrument shipping to log outbound URLs and client errors so future InvalidUri failures are visible in pod logs.
